source_text:
Homilia i in sanctum Lazarum (homilia 11)
Ἀνεγνώσθη Ἡσυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, εἰς Ἰάκωβον, τὸν
ἀδελφὸν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ∆αυὶδ τὸν θεοπάτορα.
1 Εἰ μὴ «ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτὸν γενόμενος» ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμῶν «ὑπήκοος μέχρι
θανάτου», οὐκ ἂν οἰκέται συγγενεῖς ἐχρημάτιζον, οὐκ ἂν ὁ πηλὸς πατὴρ τοῦ
κεραμέως ἐλέγετο. Ἐν τῇ Σιὼν τὴν Βηθλεὲμ ὡς παροῦσαν ἀσπάζομαι, ἐν τῇ θυγατρὶ
τὴν μητέρα βλέπω. Ἐν σοὶ δᾳδοῦχος ἀστὴρ εἷς ἀνήφθη, ἐν ταύτῃ δὲ πολλοί. Ἐκεῖνος
τοὺς Μάγους ὡδήγησεν, αὕτη Πάρθους καὶ Μήδους καὶ Ἐλαμίτας καὶ τοὺς ἐξ ἐθνῶν
πάντων τῷ φωτὶ τῆς ἀστραπῆς ἐδᾳδούχησε. Σὺ γάλα ἕλκεις ἐκ μασθῶν παρθενικῶν,
αὕτη πνεῦ-μα ἐκ κόλπων κατάγει πατρικῶν.
orientation: Hesychius, priest of Jerusalem, opens his homily on James the brother of the Lord and David the ancestor of God by contrasting Bethlehem, where Christ was born, with Zion, where the Church now receives him.
pass_a_gloss: If our savior had not humbled himself, becoming obedient as far as death, servants would not have been called kinsmen, nor would the clay have been called father of the potter. In Zion I greet Bethlehem as present; in the daughter I see the mother. In you one torch-bearing star was kindled, but in this one many. That one guided the Magi; this one with the light of lightning gave torchlight to Parthians and Medes and Elamites and those from all the nations. You draw milk from virgin breasts; this one draws down spirit from paternal bosoms.

choices.term: ἐν τῇ θυγατρὶ τὴν μητέρα βλέπω
choices.english: in the daughter I see the mother
choices.why: Keeps the literal word order and the exact nouns; the daughter is Zion, the mother is Bethlehem, as the context shows.
rejected: in the daughter I behold the mother

choices.why: Literal rendering of the compound adjective; the star is described as carrying a torch.
Literal rendering; the light is explicitly that of lightning, not just a flash.

choices.english: draws down spirit from paternal bosoms
choices.why: Keeps the verb's downward force and the literal plural 'bosoms'; the spirit comes from the Father's bosoms.
rejected: brings down the Spirit from the Father's bosom

bible_refs.note: ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτὸν γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου

pass_b_english: If our Savior had not humbled himself and become obedient to the point of death (Philippians 2:8), servants would never have been called kinsmen, nor would the clay ever have been called the father of the potter.
In Zion I greet Bethlehem as though she were present; in the daughter I see the mother.

In you one torch-bearing star was kindled, but in her many were kindled. That star guided the Magi, but she gave torchlight to Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and people from all the nations with light like lightning.
You draw milk from virgin breasts, but she draws down the Spirit from the Father's bosom.

polish.changed: Clarified the Spirit as the divine Spirit, corrected 'bosoms' to the standard singular 'bosom', and rendered the lightning phrase as 'light like lightning' to remove the nonsensical reading.

notes.why: Plural 'bosoms' is bizarre; standard biblical phrase is singular 'bosom' (John 1:18).
Lists nations from Acts 2:9 without explaining Pentecost connection.
Nonsensical phrase; likely means 'like lightning' or 'with lightning-like light'.
notes.fix: Change to 'like lightning' or 'with lightning's flash'.

notes.quote: she gave torchlight to Parthians, Medes, Elamites
notes.why: These are peoples from Acts 2:9 (Pentecost), but reader may not catch the allusion.
notes.fix: Note these are Pentecost converts from Acts 2.

notes.quote: the clay ever have been called the father of the potter
notes.why: Allusion to Isaiah 64:8 is obscure without context; clay as father of potter is paradoxical.
notes.fix: Brief note: Isaiah 64:8, 'we are the clay, you the potter.'
